title: dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics (v31)
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: reduce wasted compute from padding in continuous/dynamic batching and improve throughput/latency SLOs for mixed-length workloads. Summary: introduce a lightweight bucketing heuristic based on sequence-length quantiles with an online histogram and padding-minimization cost function; integrate bucket-aware kernel selection and KV-cache reuse to avoid cache fragmentation; add safety knobs and a feature-flagged rollout. Approach: maintain a small running histogram of request sequence lengths per serving pool, compute quantile boundaries on an interval (default 30s), derive bucket boundaries such that expected padding overhead is bounded while keeping batch fill-rate high; route incoming requests into the current active bucket and allow opportunistic cross-bucket co-batching when latency budget allows; prioritize same-bucket kernel selection to use a precompiled kernel tuned for the bucket's max seqlen; when bucket switch occurs, drain and warm KV cache to preserve cache hit-rate and fall back to per-request KV fetch if needed; expose two config knobs: target_padding_pct (default 0.15) and min_batch_fill (default 0.6). Compatibility: backward compatible with existing continuous batching; rollout behind feature flag dynamic_seqlen_bucketing; automatic fallback to legacy behavior when buckets underfilled. Tests and validation: microbenchmarks on A100 80GB and T4 pools; production canary in us-west-2 on 2 dedicated clusters. Results: end-to-end throughput improvement 12-18% on mixed chat workloads; median per-token latency similar (+/-1ms); p95 latency down ~3ms; p99 latency improved by 6-12ms on our benchmark prompt sets; empirical padding reduction ~28% across customer-like distributions. Files and changes: heuristic implementation, unit tests, integration tests, telemetry hooks, rollout toggle, docs. Rollout: staged canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks with automatic rollback on p99 regressions >10ms or error rate increase >0.5%. Related: ENG-5421 (dynamic-batching roadmap), ENG-6145 (KV cache stability).
